fields.name: All-or-Nothing Thinking
fields.description: Viewing situations in black-or-white terms, without recognizing middle ground. If things aren't perfect, they're a total failure.

fields.name: Overgeneralization
fields.description: Taking one instance or example and generalizing it to an overall pattern. Using words like 'always' or 'never'.

fields.name: Mental Filter
fields.description: Focusing exclusively on the negative aspects of a situation and filtering out the positives.

fields.name: Disqualifying the Positive
fields.description: Rejecting positive experiences by insisting they 'don’t count' for some reason or another.

fields.name: Jumping to Conclusions
fields.description: Assuming you know what others are thinking (mind reading) or predicting the future negatively (fortune telling) without evidence.

fields.name: Magnification and Minimization
fields.description: Exaggerating the importance of problems (catastrophizing) or minimizing the value of positive qualities or accomplishments.

fields.name: Emotional Reasoning
fields.description: Assuming that negative emotions reflect reality: 'I feel it, so it must be true.'

fields.name: Should Statements
fields.description: Using 'should', 'must', or 'ought to' statements to pressure yourself or others and create guilt or frustration.

fields.name: Labeling and Mislabeling
fields.description: Attaching a global, negative label to yourself or others rather than describing the specific behavior.

fields.name: Personalization
fields.description: Assuming responsibility for things outside your control or blaming yourself for events that aren't your fault.

fields.name: Control Fallacies
fields.description: Believing you are either helpless (external control) or responsible for everyone and everything (internal control).

fields.name: Fallacy of Fairness
fields.description: Believing that life should be fair and feeling upset when it isn't, even though fairness is not guaranteed.

fields.name: Blaming
fields.description: Holding others responsible for your pain, or blaming yourself for every problem.

fields.name: Heaven’s Reward Fallacy
fields.description: Expecting that self-sacrifice and hard work will inevitably be rewarded, leading to disappointment when it doesn’t happen.
